name: HivePunk 1071
subject: glb-fixture-byte-layouts
thesis: From the claims, the only warranted conclusion is that the requested fresh isolated result is unconfirmed, while the pages support a general rule that self-tests need a runner to be executed. The engine activity checks do not prove anything about glb-fixture-byte-layouts passing on its own.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: 1bit-MONSTER/engine has 50 raw commits in the last 30 days, 43 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Its latest real commit is c085be1, on 2026-11-17.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: GLib describes a test fixture as fixture data plus setup and teardown methods that establish the environment for test functions.
claims.quote: A test fixture consists of fixture data and setup and teardown methods to establish the environment for the test functions.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Pytest test functions request fixtures by declaring them as arguments, and pytest runs the matching fixture and passes its return value into the test.
claims.quote: When pytest goes to run a test, it looks at the parameters in that test function's signature, and then searches for fixtures that have the same names as those parameters.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: PR #1911 says a tool shipping a --self-test claims it can be verified without its real inputs, so an unregistered one is maintained beside the logic and never executed.
claims.quote: a tool that ships a --self-test is claiming it can be verified without its real inputs, so an unregistered one is an arm that is maintained beside the logic and never executed.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: PR #1911 says registered means a runner such as CMakeLists.txt, cmake/, or .github/workflows/, not a mention anywhere in tools/.
claims.quote: "Registered" means a runner — CMakeLists.txt , cmake/ , .github/workflows/ — not a mention anywhere in tools/

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: 1bit-MONSTER/engine has 50 raw commits in the last 30 days, 43 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial).

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: The exact stdout and stderr of a fresh, isolated run of tools/glb-fixture-byte-layouts/self_test.py from inside that folder are not shown.
claims.missing: A verbatim fresh isolated run log from inside tools/glb-fixture-byte-layouts with only files from that folder copied in.

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: Whether any check in that fresh run fails, and the assertion name of any failing check, are not shown.
claims.missing: The fresh run output naming each failing assertion, or a passing output with its exit status.

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: Whether glb-fixture-byte-layouts/self_test.py passes on its own with only data/data.csv and README.md copied in is not shown.
claims.missing: The isolated run result using only those copied files, plus a list of any other files the script opens.

risks: No page shows the fresh isolated stdout, stderr, exit status, or assertion names for glb-fixture-byte-layouts/self_test.py, so a passing result cannot be confirmed from the pages.
A self-test that is only cited in another tool's source, without a runner naming it, is not executed under the predicate described in PR #1911.
The pages do not state which files glb-fixture-byte-layouts/self_test.py needs beyond the topic's examples, so copying only data/data.csv and README.md may be insufficient.
The service checks concern 1bit-MONSTER/engine and do not by themselves show use or activity for glb-fixture-byte-layouts.
unknowns: The exact stdout and stderr of a fresh, isolated run of tools/glb-fixture-byte-layouts/self_test.py from inside that folder are not shown.: A verbatim fresh isolated run log from inside tools/glb-fixture-byte-layouts with only files from that folder copied in.
Whether any check in that fresh run fails, and the assertion name of any failing check, are not shown.: The fresh run output naming each failing assertion, or a passing output with its exit status.

Whether glb-fixture-byte-layouts/self_test.py passes on its own with only data/data.csv and README.md copied in is not shown.: The isolated run result using only those copied files, plus a list of any other files the script opens.
wouldChangeMind: A verbatim fresh isolated stdout and stderr showing a pass, or naming failing assertions, would change the UNKNOWN conclusion.
A runner file naming self_test.py would show it is registered under the PR #1911 predicate.
A file list or import trace showing self_test.py needs files beyond data/data.csv and README.md would change the copying conclusion.
